sep01-planning.summary: You and Dev worked through the Checkout Revamp rollout plan, settling on 5%, 25%, 50%, then everyone a few days apart, with the kill switch tested before each step. You also blocked out the week's Ledger Recon work, since the mismatches are driving finance nuts. Feels like a busy but good month ahead.
takeaways: Planned the Checkout Revamp rollout: 5%, 25%, 50%, then everyone.
Blocked out Ledger Recon work to fix the mismatches.
Pushed back on Dev's faster rollout; met in the middle.

sep03-recon-cutoff.summary: Most of the day was recon on the ledger job. Found the nightly 340 mismatches came from bucketing by Pacific time against settlement files cut off at midnight UTC, a bug you had partly written months ago. After a frustrating morning, pushed a fix to staging and the dry run dropped to 12 mismatches, which you'll look at tomorrow.
takeaways: Traced the ledger mismatches to a midnight UTC cutoff bucketing by Pacific time.
Pushed the fix to staging; dry run dropped from 340 mismatches to 12.
12 unexplained mismatches left to investigate tomorrow.
sep03-recon-cutoff.impact_note: Dry run mismatches down from 340 to 12.

sep08-pairing-leo.summary: Spent the afternoon pairing with Leo on his first real PR to the ledger service. Walked through the double-entry checks, and he wrote the test first on his own. Reviewed Checkout code in the morning. A normal, good day.
takeaways: Paired with Leo on his first real PR to the ledger service, test-first.
Reviewed Checkout Revamp code in the morning.

sep09-recon-clean.summary: The recon job ran clean all week, zero mismatches for seven nights, and you held off saying anything until today. The 12 from last week turned out to be refunds issued across the cutoff, which you fixed. Hannah from finance said they'll stop the manual month-end spreadsheet, saving her team two days every close, and you were really happy to close out the Ledger Reconciliation. You bought the team donuts.
takeaways: Closed out Ledger Reconciliation after a clean seven-night run.
Fixed the 12 from last week, which were refunds issued across the cutoff.

sep10-interviews.summary: Two backend interviews today: one strong on system design but hand-wavy on payments, the other a likely no since they couldn't explain their own project. Wrote up detailed feedback right after both. Interviews drain you more than coding does.
takeaways: Interviewed two backend candidates, one strong on system design but hand-wavy on payments, the other a likely no.
Wrote detailed feedback for both while it was fresh.

sep14-quiet.summary: A quiet, meeting-free day. You read through the processor's webhook docs and made notes ahead of next quarter's migration. You also reviewed three PRs, one of Leo's, and shipped a small PR cleaning up logging in the ledger service.
takeaways: Read the processor's new webhook docs and made notes for the migration.
Reviewed three PRs, including one of Leo's.
Cleaned up logging in the ledger service.

sep16-people.summary: A people-only day: three one-on-ones, an interview debrief (a hire on the second backend candidate), and no code. Leo handled his first on-call page on his own. A tense talk with Marcus settled retry-logic ownership, pending the new client. Exhausted but felt the work was useful.
takeaways: Mentoring Leo, who handled his first on-call page alone.
Plan to move Aisha to platform, starting with her manager-to-be.
Agreed payment retry ownership until the new client ships, writing it down.

sep17-five-percent.summary: Rolled Checkout Revamp out to 5% after checking the feature flag config and kill switch in staging with Priya, then flipped it at eleven. Watched dashboards all afternoon: conversion matches the old flow and no errors beyond those already on it. Cautiously happy, with 25% planned for next week if it stays quiet.
takeaways: Rolled out Checkout Revamp to 5% after staging kill-switch tests with Priya.
Conversion matches the old flow and no new errors so far.
Going to 25% next week if it stays quiet.
sep17-five-percent.impact_note: rolled out to 5% with conversion matching the old flow

sep18-dashboard-p95.summary: Profiled the slow transactions page on Merchant Dashboard and found a missing composite index on merchant ID and created-at, plus full refund history being fetched though it's never shown. Adding the index and making the refund fetch lazy dropped p95 from 1.8 seconds to about 600 milliseconds in production. Dev posted it in the product channel and called it huge for merchant NPS; you want to write up the profiling approach to share with the team.
takeaways: Cut Merchant Dashboard transactions p95 from 1.8s to 600ms in production.
Added a missing composite index and made refund history lazy.
Dev called it huge for the merchant NPS; you want to write up the approach.

sep21-double-charge.summary: Checkout went to 50% this morning and support flagged double charges within an hour. The idempotency key was regenerating on retry, so 41 customers were charged twice. Rolled back in 20 minutes and finance refunded everyone by afternoon. Wrote the incident timeline; postmortem is Wednesday. Priya stayed late to go through the retry path, which was appreciated.
takeaways: Rolled back the 50% checkout rollout after double charges hit 41 customers.
Wrote the incident timeline; postmortem set for Wednesday.
Priya stayed late to walk the retry path line by line.
sep21-double-charge.impact_note: 41 customers double-charged, all refunded by afternoon

sep22-fix-and-meeting.summary: Wrote the retry bug fix so the key is generated once per checkout attempt and persisted, plus a test simulating the processor timeout. Priya reviewed it and caught a retry-after-session-refresh case, which you fixed together. The afternoon was rougher: Grace asked whether to pause the rollout for a month, and you got defensive. You landed on returning to 50% Thursday if the postmortem goes okay.
takeaways: Wrote the retry bug fix, with a test simulating the processor timeout.
Priya caught a retry-after-session-refresh case; fixed it together.
Rollout going back to 50% Thursday if the postmortem goes okay.

sep23-postmortem.summary: The postmortem this morning went fine and stayed blameless. It produced three action items: the timeout test goes into the standard checkout suite, retries get their own dashboard, and a 5% canary before any big jump. You own the first, already done since yesterday, and spent the rest of the day on reviews.
takeaways: Postmortem this morning was fine and blameless, came out with three action items.

That closes out roughly six months of work. Grace called out the retry fix in the launch channel, which meant a lot after Tuesday, and you're genuinely relieved.
